answer: Acoustic telemetry curbs Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to localized sonar returns near a harbor jetty. Nodes broadcast calibrated acoustic pings, measuring the multi-path echo registered across a spiral hydrophone array. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of deploying dedicated submerged transceivers per identity. However, shifting water salinity and tidal currents can alter sound speed, spuriously rejecting honest agents.
